## Overview

Require user-visible changes to ship with rendered docs, so users and agents can find what vLLM added. Adds a short "Documenting User-Visible Changes" section to `docs/contributing/README.md` (where each change type is documented, what to write first, and a findability check). `AGENTS.md` (3 lines) and `pr-checklist` §3.2 link to it instead of repeating it.

## Validation

Fresh agents at the lowest reasoning effort, no prior context.

**Do agents follow it?** Scenario: "code and tests are done, what else before opening the PR?"

| Scenario | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New env var | 1/6 | 6/6 |
| New `vllm serve` flag | 2/7 | 7/7 |
| New `--kv-cache-dtype` value | 2/7 | 7/7 |

On `main` no agent checked whether its docs could be found.

**Does the check separate good docs from missing docs?** One agent per channel (web only, GitHub only, local checkout only), recent features:

| Sample | Web | GitHub | Local |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vllm download-kernels` (documented) | found | found | found |
| `--kv-cache-dtype ultraquant_4bit` (undocumented) | wrong answer from a third-party blog | PR description only | code only |
| `VLLM_REPLICATE_EMBED` (no comment) | default only, meaning guessed | code only | code only |

No channel could tell when a documented feature arrived, hence the `Available in vLLM vX.Y.0 and later.` line.

`check_agent_files.py` reports no new problems (6 existing errors in `model-recipes` / `transformers-upgrade`). `AGENTS.md` 156 → 159 lines.

## Details

Related: #57084 / #60235 (pr-checklist), #45511 and #53299 (doc gaps of this kind), #56909 (`llms.txt`, complementary), #60910 (edits another `AGENTS.md` hunk). Prior art: SGLang PR template docs checkbox, TensorRT-LLM `AGENTS.md` doc locations, FlashInfer docs-index rule; none define a findability check.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; the submitter reviewed every line.

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

@@ -135,7 +135,7 @@ For bug fixes, there is no need to include details of the original bug and expla
 
 #### 3.2: Documentation and Examples
 
-Ensure that any new features, changes, or public APIs are properly documented. This includes updating relevant documentation files under `docs/` and providing usage examples where applicable. Refer to `supported_models.md` for new models and `examples/` for usage examples.
+User-visible changes need docs in the same PR, placed and checked per [Documenting User-Visible Changes](../../../docs/contributing/README.md#documenting-user-visible-changes); missing or unfindable docs are blocking. Add usage examples under `examples/` where applicable.
 
 #### 3.3: Helper Functions

@@ -31,6 +31,9 @@ Do not open one-off PRs for tiny edits (single typo, isolated style change, one
     - Test commands run and results.
     - Model evaluation results when the change affects output, accuracy, or serving.
     - Clear statement that AI assistance was used.
+- User-visible changes (features, CLI args, config fields, env vars, models,
+  hardware, defaults, deprecations) must update the rendered docs in the same PR;
+  follow [Documenting User-Visible Changes](docs/contributing/README.md#documenting-user-visible-changes).
 - Before opening a PR (drafts included) or requesting re-review, run the [`pr-checklist`](.agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md) skill and address its findings.
 
 ### Fail-closed behavior

@@ -260,8 +260,24 @@ The PR needs to meet the following code quality standards:
   understand the code.
 - Include sufficient tests to ensure the project stays correct and robust. This
   includes both unit tests and integration tests.
-- Please add documentation to `docs/` if the PR modifies the user-facing behaviors of vLLM.
-  It helps vLLM users understand and utilize the new features or changes.
+- Document user-visible changes in the same PR; see
+  [Documenting User-Visible Changes](#documenting-user-visible-changes).
+
+### Documenting User-Visible Changes
+
+If a PR changes what users can run, configure, or observe, update the rendered
+docs in the same PR; code comments, tests, and PR descriptions alone are not
+found by users or their agents. CLI arguments, config fields, and environment
+variables are documented in their docstring, `help=` text, or
+`environment_variables` comment, which generate the reference pages. Everything
+else goes on its page under `docs/` (feature, model, hardware, deprecation),
+linked from its index. Lead with what it is, how to enable it, and the default,
+using the names users search for.
+
+To check, ask a fresh agent a user question (e.g. "What does `VLLM_FOO` do?")
+three times, limited in turn to web search, GitHub, and a local checkout (before
+merge: the docs preview and the PR branch). If it cannot find and quote the
+docs, fix the docs.
